findings.finding: The null-set argument needed the implication from a unique noncritical minimizer to a neighborhood of unique minimizing branches, and the outgoing regularity statement needed one open spacetime locus with null complements on every slice.
findings.resolution: Rademacher and Sard give differentiable noncritical endpoints. First variation fixes every minimizing terminal covector and phase-ODE uniqueness fixes the path. Bounded initial lifts and a convergent subsequence contradict failure of inverse-branch stability. Positive smooth volume densities transfer chart null sets to the selected slice measure. The theorem now exports spacetime local Lipschitz regularity and the common regular locus explicitly.
findings.standard_background: Morgan-Tian, Claim 7.22 and Corollary 7.24, pp. 161-162, within Theorem 7.13, pp. 156-164. Sard applies to the smooth full exponential; Rademacher applies to Lipschitz chart representatives. Neither is used on a merely arbitrary measurable function.

findings.finding: An almost-everywhere Laplacian bound does not by itself give the claimed distributional inequality. The earlier prose named semiconcavity but omitted the weighted-operator limit that justifies this step.
findings.resolution: The revised proof accounts for the Christoffel gradient term, subtracts a quadratic to obtain concavity, and explains convolution with a uniform upper Hessian and gradient bound. For rho*Delta=div(rho*B^{-1}d), this yields a common upper bound on Delta of the smooth approximations. Second jets converge on the full-measure regular locus; upper Fatou plus the fixed smooth-test Green identity transfers the upper bound, followed by a finite partition of unity. Both signs are checked using 2*partial_tau(l)+|grad l|^2-R+l/tau=0. Slice measures are explicit in the display.
findings.standard_background: Morgan-Tian, Theorem 7.13, pp. 156-164. The proof develops the singular-Hessian and smoothing step rather than treating integration by parts across the cut locus as automatic.

findings.finding: The old upper-barrier paragraph described a short terminal joining construction, which was not the current producer. Several theorem-type and page locators were also incorrect.
findings.resolution: The proof now constructs one smooth comparison family realizing Y_i(s)=(s/c)P_i(s), with D_s P_i=-2s Ric# P_i. Its endpoint-time map is invertible even at a critical minimizing exponential. The normalized comparison action has exact zero residual at contact. The index-form defect argument explains tensor equality; the Jacobi kernel is explicitly endpoint-zero. Checked square-root coefficients, the four curvature slots, the fixed-spatial-point time derivative in H, all K cancellations, and the positive-start C_a and shifted Harnack weight. The original 2*sqrt(b) normalization is retained.
findings.current_path_correction: The historical helper anchor ReducedLength/Barrier/ComparisonBarrier.lean is not a current path. The four Barrier files above supply the current construction; the historical author list remains preserved at its original pin.
findings.standard_background: Morgan-Tian, Propositions 6.37 and 6.43, pp. 123-129; Lemma 6.49 and Theorem 6.50, p. 131; Corollary 6.51, p. 132; Propositions 6.56 and 6.59, pp. 133-139; Proposition 7.8, pp. 152-154. Items 6.52-6.55 are not a series of Claims. The positive-start display follows the current source's shifted weight, not an unqualified transcription of the book's K notation.

findings.finding: The proof did not distinguish the globally continuous raw action weight from its regular-domain indicator, and it jumped from equality to the metric pairing and stationary identification.
findings.resolution: A strict-subslab phase bound explains the full smooth exponential family. Maximal integrated weight gives a conull regular source; continuity of the raw action weight gives an everywhere positive differential. Open-dense injectivity and existence of minimizing lifts give a global diffeomorphism. The logarithmic weight derivative is exactly minus the sharp Laplacian defect. Equality yields Ric+Hess(l)=g/(2s); the pairing ODE a'=a/s with its initial coefficient gives pullback metric 4s*g(T). Its determinant and weight equality give l=|Z|^2, and first variation gives the radial velocity which cancels in the rescaled exponential. Continuity includes both slab endpoints. The small-time indicator limit is linked to the later ODE/action comparison, which does not assume a volume theorem.
findings.source_comparison: Morgan-Tian, Theorem 6.80 and Proposition 6.81, pp. 145-146; Theorem 7.26, p. 165; Proposition 7.27, pp. 166-167. The last proposition uses a selfsimilar-flow/curvature argument. The chapter instead develops the implemented exponential-pairing and stationary-map argument; no novelty claim is made.

findings.finding: The transition to generalized path calculus did not explicitly require the intrinsic Ricci equation, and the generalized zero-time volume statement did not clearly specify the stable image being integrated.
findings.resolution: Added the intrinsic Ricci equation together with the supplied gauge and leafwise data. The carrier, selected horizontal metric, ordinary pullback metric and clock are the same throughout. Defined generalized volume on the image of a measurable stable source and restricted the zero-time assertion to the full stable image. Whole-past-slab curvature remains necessary in the small-time competitor-confinement argument. Ordinary full-slice capture retains its ordinary M08-M10 inputs; no generalized full-slice null-complement assertion was added.
findings.standard_background: Morgan-Tian, Definitions 3.34-3.36 and Remark 3.37, pp. 59-60; Definition 3.40, p. 61; Proposition 7.5, pp. 151-152. Parabolic action scaling is sqrt(Q), reduced length is unchanged, and the density and volume factors cancel; Euclidean volume remains (4*pi)^(n/2).

findings.finding: The existing speed and strict-displacement argument used a dimension-only scalar-gradient bound without explaining how the compactness hypothesis of the local derivative theorem is supplied on the actual cylinder.
findings.resolution: The rescaled unit cylinder has a compact initial-metric ball of radius exp(-n)/8 about every terminal half-ball point, by metric comparison and the terminal interior buffer. The ordinary local derivative estimate on the last half-cylinder gives A/r^3 after scaling back. The square-root speed bound integrates to 5r/12<r/2, and compact inverse-chart continuation prevents an earlier maximal lift endpoint. The source cutoff |Z|^2<=1/(64*epsilon), scalar lower bound, measure distortion, 2+1 volume split and fixed choice 3*epsilon^(n/2)<c retain their coefficients. No completeness of the generalized slice is inferred.
findings.standard_background: Morgan-Tian, Proposition 8.2, pp. 170-171; Lemma 8.3, p. 171; Corollary 8.4 and Claim 8.5, p. 172; Claims 8.6-8.8, pp. 173-174; Lemma 8.9, pp. 175-176. These are not all Lemmas. The compactness buffer is the source's corrected application of the ordinary local estimate.

cross_chapter_review.result: No mismatch found in these outgoing interfaces. Ancient-models produces a uniform curvature bound on each finite past slab and takes tau_max=tau_i+1 to use interior-time reduced-length minima. Its Harnack input gives K>=-L, hence |grad l|^2+R<=3l/tau and partial_tau(l)>=R-2l/tau. The first variation gives its Hamilton-Jacobi identity. The common regular spacetime locus is slice-null, so its Fubini arguments use the actual weak derivatives; the signed flux bound follows from Delta(l)<=-partial_tau(l)+(n/2-l)/tau. Exact rescaling cancels density and measure factors. Its limiting potential is not asserted to be reduced length from an unconstructed limiting basepoint. Its own argument owns the passage to weak heat equality and regularity.
